The EmporiumDazed and ConfusedLast day of school. Nobody's going home.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersMoon tower chipsOnion chive dip and thick chips. Slater climbs the tower.How to make it2 brown onions, sliced1 tbsp vegetable oil300g sour cream1 small bunch chives1 big bag thick-cut potato chipssalt, to tasteCook the onions slowly in the oil until deep brown.Cool and chop.Fold into the sour cream with salt and chopped chives.Serve with the chips.Freshman paddle pretzelsPretzel rods dipped in peanut butter, then milk chocolateHow to make it100g peanut butter1 tbsp honey20 pretzel rods150g milk chocolateWarm the peanut butter with the honey.Dip the pretzels halfway and chill.Melt the chocolate and dip the pretzels again.Set on baking paper.Emporium chilli butter beer nutsPool hall nuts, mind the paint on O'BannionHow to make itAs written, serves 4Salted peanuts and pretzel twists roasted in chilli butter, smoked paprika and a little brown sugar until glossy and crunchy, served warm in paper cups.Melt 50g butter with 1 tsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp brown sugar and 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce.Toss with 250g salted roasted peanuts and 150g pretzel twists on a lined tray.Bake at 160°C for 15 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the coating is dry and glossy.Cool for 10 minutes so they crisp up, then tip into paper cups.Frito pie with Texas chilliAlright, alright, alright. Wooderson's order.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsEmporium chicken fried steakBreaded minute steak shallow fried, with peppery cream gravyHow to make it4 thin beef minute steaks150g plain flour2 eggs, beaten500ml vegetable oil500ml full cream milk1 tbsp cracked black peppersalt, to tastePound the steaks thin and season the flour.Dip in seasoned flour, then egg, then flour again.Shallow fry in about 1cm oil until golden each side.For the gravy, cook some flour in a little of the oil, whisk in the milk and simmer until thick. Season with lots of pepper.Texas salt and pepper brisket with picklesBrisket after mailbox baseball. Mind the gun.How to make itAs written, serves 4Brisket rubbed with coarse salt and cracked pepper, roasted low for ten hours until it wobbles, sliced thick on white bread with pickles, onion and barbecue sauce.Rub a 2.5kg beef brisket with 2 tbsp coarse salt and 2 tbsp cracked black pepper and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight.Roast fat side up on a rack at 120°C for 9 to 10 hours until the thickest part reaches 95°C.Wrap in foil and baking paper and rest 1 hour.Slice thick against the grain and serve on soft white bread with sliced dill pickles, thin raw onion and 250ml smoky barbecue sauce.SweetsLast day of '76 sweet tea ice blocksBlack tea sweetened with sugar and lemon, frozen on sticksHow to make it4 black tea bags750ml boiling water100g caster sugar1 lemonSteep the tea bags in the boiling water, then remove.Stir in the sugar while hot and add the lemon juice. Cool.Pour into ice block moulds and add sticks.Freeze until solid.DrinksWooderson's micheladaCold lager with lime, tomato juice and hot sauce, chilli salt rimHow to make it1 tbsp salt1 tsp chilli powder4 limes120ml tomato juice12 dashes of hot sauce8 dashes of Worcestershire sauce1.3 L cold lager (4 x 330ml)4 cups iceMix the salt with the chilli powder on a saucer. Rub the glass rims with lime and dip in the salt.Fill the glasses with ice. Add lime juice, tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire to each.Top slowly with cold lager, stir once and serve with a lime wedge.Lone Star beer, ice coldJust keep livin', L-I-V-I-N.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
